metadata.title: Rubrik Quarantine Files
metadata.description: This playbook is an HTTP Request-triggered child playbook that quarantines a batch of files reported by a Rubrik Security Cloud DSPM violation. It is called by the RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation playbook with the whole files array in a single call and iterates internally, so it runs once per incident instead of once per file. It branches on objectType into three paths: ONEDRIVE files are quarantined via Microsoft Graph (the analyst is asked once per run for a share link to a single destination quarantine folder via a Teams Adaptive Card; that link is resolved once up front with GET /v1.0/shares/{link}/driveItem into a destination driveId and item id, so the destination is decoupled from each file's source drive and no per-file folder lookup or create is performed. Each file is then resolved directly by drive and path - the drive from the RSC snappable identity, driveOwnerUpn for OneDrive or siteUrl for SharePoint, and the path from filePath/nativePath - downloaded, uploaded into the single destination folder with @microsoft.graph.conflictBehavior=rename so same-named files from different drives do not overwrite each other, and the source deleted only after a confirmed upload; if the file cannot be resolved at that exact path the file is reported Failed and is never matched by a tenant-wide search); NTFS (Windows Fileset) files are quarantined via Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (the device is resolved by physicalHost, each file's SHA1 is resolved via advanced hunting scoped by DeviceId, FileName and FolderPath, and a StopAndQuarantineFile machine action is created and polled for up to 20 minutes). Note that RSC supplies physicalHost only on SecurityViolation events, so Windows Fileset files arriving from a Classification event are reported Failed with an explanatory message rather than silently skipped; any other objectType returns NotImplemented. A single app registration (client id/secret in Key Vault) authenticates both Microsoft Graph and MDE; only the OAuth2 token scope differs per branch. The playbook returns { status, results: [ { filename, status, newLocation, error } ] } to the caller.
prerequisites: 1. A single Azure AD app registration is used for BOTH Microsoft Graph and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Grant it (all admin-consented):
a. Microsoft Graph APPLICATION permissions: Files.ReadWrite.All, Sites.ReadWrite.All, User.Read.All.
b. WindowsDefenderATP (Microsoft Defender for Endpoint) APPLICATION permissions: Machine.ReadWrite.All (or Machine.StopAndQuarantine) and AdvancedQuery.Read.All.
2. Store the app registration credentials in Key Vault and obtain the Key Vault name and tenantId.
a. Create a Key Vault with a unique name.

b. Go to KeyVault -> secrets, click Generate/import and create TWO secrets using EXACTLY these names (they are fixed in the playbook and are not deployment parameters): 'Graph-App-ClientId' holding the app registration's Application (client) ID, and 'Graph-App-ClientSecret' holding its client secret VALUE. The same credentials authenticate both Microsoft Graph and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
NOTE: Make sure the Permission model in the Access Configuration of the Key Vault is set to 'Vault access policy'. If not, change it to 'Vault access policy'.
3. For the ONEDRIVE branch, a Microsoft Teams team and channel are required for the Adaptive Card that collects the quarantine folder share link.

3a. Create the destination quarantine folder in OneDrive or SharePoint before running the playbook and have its share link ready (Share -> Copy link). All files in a run are moved into that single folder regardless of which drive they came from, and same-named files are renamed rather than overwritten. The app registration must be able to read the link, so prefer a link scoped to people in your organization over a link restricted to named individuals. Exclude this quarantine folder from DSPM scan scope, otherwise the quarantined copies are scanned again and raise fresh violations for files that were just remediated.

4. For the NTFS branch, the target file shares must be hosted on devices onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and resolvable by their physicalHost / computerDnsName. RSC supplies physicalHost only on SecurityViolation events; Windows Fileset files arriving from a Classification event cannot be quarantined and are reported Failed with an explanatory message. KNOWN LIMITATION: the file's SHA1 is resolved from the most recent DeviceFileEvents record (Defender retains roughly 30 days) and StopAndQuarantineFile is keyed by that hash. If the file has since been modified or deleted, Defender reports the action as successful even though nothing was quarantined.

5. This playbook is a prerequisite for the RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation playbook and must be deployed first, in the same resource group. RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation calls this playbook as a sub-playbook (via its RubrikQuarantineFilesPlaybookName parameter) once per incident to quarantine the violation files.
postDeployment: **a. Authorize connections**
Once deployment is complete, authorize each connection.
1. Go to your logic app -> API connections -> Select the Teams connection resource.
2. Go to General -> edit API connection.
3. Click Authorize.
4. Sign in.
5. Click Save.
6. The Key Vault connection uses the managed identity and does not require an interactive sign-in.
**b. Assign Role to comment on and update incidents (if the caller requires it)**
1. Go to Log Analytics Workspace -> <your workspace> -> Access Control -> Add.
2. Add role assignment.
3. Assignment type: Job function roles.
4. Role: Microsoft Sentinel Responder.
5. Members: select managed identity for assigned access to and add your logic app as member.
6. Click on review + assign.
**c. Add Access policy in Key Vault**
Add an access policy for the playbook's managed identity to read the app-registration secrets.
1. Go to logic app -> <your logic app> -> Identity -> System assigned managed identity and copy the Object (principal) ID.
2. Go to keyvaults -> <your keyvault> -> Access policies -> Create.
3. Select Get on secrets permissions. Click next.
4. In the principal section, search by the copied object ID. Click next.
5. Click review + create.
**d. Grant the app registration API permissions**
1. In Entra ID -> App registrations -> <your app> -> API permissions, add the Microsoft Graph and WindowsDefenderATP application permissions listed in the prerequisites and grant admin consent.
2. For the NTFS branch, ensure the file-share hosts are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and resolvable by their physicalHost / computerDnsName.
**e. Configurations in Microsoft Sentinel**
1. This playbook has an HTTP Request trigger and is invoked by RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation; it does not attach directly to an automation rule.

2. Deploy this playbook before RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation. When deploying RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation, set its RubrikQuarantineFilesPlaybookName parameter to this Logic App's name so it can call this sub-playbook.

inputs.name: Failure_Message
inputs.value: Failed to acquire a Microsoft Graph token (status @{coalesce(outputs('Get_Graph_Token')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Verify the app registration credentials in Key Vault and the tenant id.

body.text: Paste a share link to the destination quarantine folder. @{length(coalesce(triggerBody()?['files'], json('[]')))} file(s) will be moved into that single folder, whichever drive (OneDrive or SharePoint document library) each file came from. Create the folder in OneDrive or SharePoint first, use Share / Copy link, and paste the link here. Files with the same name are renamed rather than overwritten.

body.label: Quarantine folder share link
body.errorMessage: Please paste the share link of the destination quarantine folder.

inputs.name: Failure_Message
inputs.value: @{if(empty(trim(coalesce(variables('Quarantine_Share_Link'), ''))), 'No quarantine folder share link was provided by the analyst. No files were quarantined.', concat('Could not resolve the quarantine folder from the supplied share link (Graph status ', string(coalesce(outputs('Resolve_quarantine_share_link')?['statusCode'], 'none')), '). Ensure the link points to a folder (not a file), that it has not expired, and that the app registration can read it. No files were quarantined. ', string(coalesce(body('Resolve_quarantine_share_link'), ''))))}

value.error: No drive owner UPN or site URL was supplied for this file, and no file path is available; cannot resolve the target drive without a tenant-wide search. Ensure the calling playbook sends driveOwnerUpn (OneDrive) or siteUrl (SharePoint) from the RSC snappable.
No filePath (RSC nativePath) was supplied for this file; cannot resolve it by path. Source NOT modified.

Could not resolve the OneDrive for owner '@{items('For_each_file')?['driveOwnerUpn']}' (Graph status @{coalesce(outputs('Get_user_drive')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Verify the user exists, has a provisioned OneDrive, and that the app registration holds Files.ReadWrite.All. @{string(coalesce(body('Get_user_drive'), ''))}
No document library on site '@{items('For_each_file')?['siteUrl']}' matches the first segment of the file path '@{variables('Item_Path')}' (by name or URL). Nothing was modified.

Resolved the SharePoint site but could not enumerate its document libraries (Graph status @{coalesce(outputs('Batch_get_site_drives')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). @{string(coalesce(body('Batch_get_site_drives'), ''))}

Could not resolve the SharePoint site '@{items('For_each_file')?['siteUrl']}' (Graph status @{coalesce(outputs('Batch_get_site_by_url')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Verify the site URL from the RSC snappable and that the app registration holds Sites.ReadWrite.All. @{string(coalesce(body('Batch_get_site_by_url'), ''))}

File not found at path '@{variables('Item_Path_Final')}' in document library '@{coalesce(variables('Matched_Drive')?['name'], variables('Drive_Name'), 'default')}' (drive '@{variables('Target_Drive_Id')}') (Graph status @{coalesce(outputs('Get_item_by_path')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). The playbook resolves files by exact drive and path and does not fall back to a tenant-wide search, so nothing was modified. Verify the RSC nativePath matches the current location of the file. @{string(coalesce(body('Get_item_by_path'), ''))}

@if(and(greaterOrEquals(coalesce(outputs('Delete_source_file')?['statusCode'], 0), 200), less(coalesce(outputs('Delete_source_file')?['statusCode'], 0), 300)), '', concat('Uploaded to quarantine but failed to delete the source (Graph status ', string(coalesce(outputs('Delete_source_file')?['statusCode'], 'none')), '); delete manually.'))

The server-side copy to the quarantine folder '@{variables('Quarantine_Folder_Label')}' did not complete within 10 minutes (copy status '@{coalesce(body('Get_copy_status')?['status'], '')}'). Source NOT deleted. @{string(coalesce(body('Get_copy_status')?['error'], ''))}

The server-side copy to the quarantine folder '@{variables('Quarantine_Folder_Label')}' could not be started (Graph status @{coalesce(outputs('Copy_to_quarantine')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Source NOT deleted. @{string(coalesce(body('Copy_to_quarantine')?['error'], ''))}

inputs.name: Failure_Message
inputs.value: @{if(equals(length(body('Filter_failed_results')), 0), '', concat(string(length(body('Filter_failed_results'))), ' of ', string(length(variables('Results'))), ' file(s) failed to quarantine. ', string(body('Filter_failed_results'))))}

inputs.name: Failure_Message
inputs.value: Failed to acquire a Microsoft Defender for Endpoint token (status @{coalesce(outputs('Get_MDE_Token')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Verify the app registration has WindowsDefenderATP application permissions and the credentials in Key Vault.

value.error: No physicalHost was provided for this Windows Fileset file, so the MDE device could not be resolved and the file was not quarantined. RSC supplies physicalHost only on SecurityViolation events (policyViolation.resourceMetadata.metadata.physicalHost); Classification events do not carry it. Quarantine this file from a SecurityViolation event, or quarantine it manually in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

Could not resolve the file-share host '@{items('For_each_ntfs_file')?['physicalHost']}' in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (status @{coalesce(outputs('Get_MDE_Machine')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Ensure the host is onboarded to MDE.

body.Query: DeviceFileEvents | where DeviceId == @'@{replace(coalesce(variables('MDE_Machine_Id'), ''), '''', '''''')}' and FileName =~ @'@{replace(coalesce(items('For_each_ntfs_file')?['filename'], ''), '''', '''''')}' and FolderPath =~ @'@{replace(coalesce(items('For_each_ntfs_file')?['nativePath'], items('For_each_ntfs_file')?['filePath'], ''), '''', '''''')}' and isnotempty(SHA1) | top 1 by Timestamp desc | project SHA1

value.error: Could not resolve a SHA1 for the file via MDE advanced hunting (status @{coalesce(outputs('Run_advanced_hunting_for_sha1')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). The file may not have been observed by MDE on host '@{items('For_each_ntfs_file')?['physicalHost']}'; not quarantined.
Failed to create the MDE StopAndQuarantineFile action (status @{coalesce(outputs('Create_stop_and_quarantine')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). @{string(coalesce(body('Create_stop_and_quarantine'), ''))}
MDE StopAndQuarantineFile action did not succeed within the timeout (final status @{coalesce(body('Get_action_status')?['status'], 'Unknown')}).

inputs.name: Failure_Message
inputs.value: @{if(equals(length(body('Filter_failed_results_ntfs')), 0), '', concat(string(length(body('Filter_failed_results_ntfs'))), ' of ', string(length(variables('Results'))), ' NTFS file(s) failed to quarantine. ', string(body('Filter_failed_results_ntfs'))))}
